title: Make Mint blocks authoritative hard scheduling walls
objective: Replace hardcoded/fallback Mint block generation and soft movable-zone behavior with one authoritative source: effective Mint allotment plus selected session IDs. Derive capacity, Mint rows, shadow intents, calendar writes, and readback expectations from that source. Make selected Mint intervals immutable/hard walls for judgment, backend validation, and frontend overflow. Retire any rule that allows Mint tasks before/inside selected Mint sessions unless explicitly permitted by a fixture contract.

diagnosis.root_cause: Two compounding defects: (a) capacity reserved effective_allotment_minutes/30 Mint blocks while _SCHED_DEFAULTS injected the legacy aggregate 'Minting' row with a hardcoded n=2 (60 minutes) whenever no saved sessions list existed — a 300-minute allotment showed 10 capacity blocks but placed only 2; (b) selected Mint session rows were immutable in output but never placement walls — an assigned task could overlap a selected Mint interval, and the only window rule was the upper-bound-only frozen contract 14 allowance.
diagnosis.observed_failure: BusyCal showed Mint output intervals and assigned tasks overlapping them; capacity and the injected row disagreed (300 minutes of capacity vs 2 blocks placed).
diagnosis.fix: The effective Mint allotment (resolved day-semantics contract, dated override fallback) derives the legacy aggregate Minting row's size (allotment/30 blocks — the same number capacity reserves). Selected Mint session intervals become HARD walls: sequence.validate_sequence rejects any assigned row overlapping one (no overlap-grant escape), and the frontend overflow free-gap scan treats them as walls like calendar walls and immutable pins.

acceptance_criteria_met: Effective Mint allotment and selected session IDs produce the same Mint capacity/rows/intents: capacity reserves effective_allotment_minutes/30 blocks; the legacy aggregate row is now derived from the same allotment (300 minutes → 10 blocks, duration 300); selected-session rows are 1 block each and their total equals allotment/30 when in sync; shadow/write intents inherit the sequence rows unchanged (test_session_row_total_matches_effective_allotment_capacity, test_aggregate_minting_row_uses_effective_allotment, route-level test_sequence_injects_allotment_derived_minting_row).

No fallback hardcoded 2-block Mint injection when configured allotment is 300 minutes: build_schedulable_blocks uses the effective allotment when present; the _SCHED_DEFAULTS n=2 default survives only when NO allotment context exists (legacy no-preset callers), preserving test_weekday_defaults.

Assigned tasks cannot be placed inside selected Mint intervals; over-assignment is explicit: validate_sequence hard-rejects any assigned row overlapping a selected Mint interval (no grant escape), while a row ending exactly at the interval's start or beginning exactly at its end is allowed as touching, not overlap (test_assigned_row_overlapping_selected_mint_session_is_hard_rejection, test_mint_wall_is_not_softened_by_an_overlap_grant, test_back_to_back_boundary_is_allowed).

Mint rows are immutable/hard walls across backend and frontend validation: backend rejects overlaps at validate_sequence and /validate-sequence (route test); frontend overflow free-gap placement skips selected Mint intervals via the new mintWalls helper wired into planOverflow in controller.autoSequence; the mint row itself is exempt from its own wall (test_mint_row_itself_is_not_a_violation).

Existing calendar-wall, overflow, classification, and setup-gate tests remain green: FEEDBACK-02/05 calendar scenario suite, FEEDBACK-03 overflow suite, capacity/classification suites, FEEDBACK-24 setup-gate suite, sequence/validate-sequence/shadow/external-sources suites all pass (targeted run 284 passed; full backend 1253 passed).
Fixtures/fakes only: zero live POST, zero calendar/Todoist writes, zero restart, zero commit. All tests use synthetic data and monkeypatched judgment.

changes.behavior: Add _effective_mint_minutes(day_setup, resolved_day_semantics) — the effective Mint allotment, preferring the resolved day-semantics contract then the dated work_allotment_minutes runstate override, else None (legacy no-allotment). build_schedulable_blocks accepts resolved_day_semantics and derives the legacy aggregate Minting row's n from the effective allotment (allotment/30) instead of the hardcoded _SCHED_DEFAULTS n=2; the window-remainder cap and explicit-on re-include behavior are unchanged.

Add selected_mint_walls(items) — rows whose item carries mint_session plus a placement window become hard wall spans. validate_sequence rejects any non-Mint row overlapping a selected Mint interval as a HARD error (no overlap-grant escape; the Mint row's own id is exempt; back-to-back touch allowed). The upper-bound window backstop (frozen contract 14) is preserved.

POST /sequence and /validate-sequence pass resolved_day_semantics (body.day_semantics, getattr-guarded) into build_schedulable_blocks so the effective Mint allotment reaches schedulable-row injection.

SEQUENCE_SYSTEM_PROMPT METADATA-AWARE PLACEMENT section: selected Mint sessions are now framed as HARD placement walls — only the Mint row occupies its exact window, no other assigned row may overlap it (prompt-side hardening so the single billed call avoids producing a hard-rejected proposal).

Add mintWalls(rows) — selected Mint session intervals as WallInterval[], identified by the server's mint_session wire marker or the canonical 'Mint …' id prefix; the legacy aggregate 'Minting' row is not a wall. planOverflow callers pass them in the walls list; docstrings updated.
controller.autoSequence passes [...calendarWalls(...), ...mintWalls(rows)] into planOverflow so dropped-row overflow placement never stages a row over a selected Mint interval.

New suite (14 tests): TestMintAllotmentDerivation (effective-allotment derivation, dated override, legacy default preserved, zero suppress, sessions win over aggregate, session total == capacity), TestMintWallsHardValidation (overlap hard rejection, mint row exempt, back-to-back touch, no grant escape, upper-bound backstop), TestSequenceRouteMintDerivation (route injects allotment-derived row), TestValidateSequenceMintWalls (route rejects overlap, allows clean rows).
Add mintWalls tests (metadata rows, id-prefix fallback, non-Mint/zero-length ignored) and planOverflow Mint-wall avoidance tests (row moved after wall, infeasibility reported).
Add FEEDBACK-25 controller-wiring test: a canned sequence with a selected Mint session at the anchor plus dropped rows — overflow rows never overlap the Mint interval.

preserved_semantics: Legacy aggregate Minting row with no allotment context keeps the historical 2-block default (test_weekday_defaults) — the hardcoded fallback is retired only when an effective allotment exists.

Frozen contract 14 upper-bound window check for placement-window items is preserved; the locked-contract suite (test_locked_contract_red.py) still passes — its before-window mint-row case is the explicit fixture-contract permission the task's retire-clause allows.
The window-remainder cap (skill 1249) and explicit-on re-include still operate; a zero allotment still suppresses the legacy row.
Mint capacity computation (_capacity_frame) is unchanged; rows now agree with it instead of diverging.
No event immutability or no-writer fixture contract is touched; quarantine/ignored calendar exclusion (contract 17) is untouched.

residual_limitations: The frozen contract 14 upper-bound-only allowance for a placement-window row's own placement remains (the mint row is merged to its exact window after judgment, so the lower bound is enforced by merge; the locked-contract test is the explicit fixture-contract permission the retire-clause allows).

The legacy aggregate Minting row (no selected sessions) remains a model-movable row sized by the effective allotment — it is not a hard wall because it has no fixed interval; only user-selected session intervals are walls.

planOverflow infeasibility reason text labels all wall kinds as 'calendar wall' when mint walls share the list — placement correctness is exact; the wording is shared with the FEEDBACK-03 calendar-wall test assertion.
The judgment prompt change is prompt-side hardening only; enforcement is the deterministic validate_sequence wall (a violating proposal is rejected, never silently accepted).
